summary: Stipendium Hungaricum is the Hungarian government's scholarship for bachelor's, master's and PhD study in Hungary. It pays tuition, a monthly stipend, a housing contribution and medical insurance. You must be nominated by your country's 'sending partner' (for Nigeria, the Federal Scholarship Board), so you apply twice: on the Hungarian portal and to your sending partner.
lookfor: Your sending partner's nomination — without it you cannot advance
A clear, well-matched choice of two eligible programmes
Your result in the host university's entrance exam or interview (minimum 56 out of 100)
A complete, readable set of documents and a convincing motivation letter
Academic record and language ability for the programme
cycle: The 2027/28 call had not been published on 7 Oct 2026. Last cycle: call published mid-November, deadline 15 January (2 p.m. CET), nominations by end of February, university exams March–May, results end of June/early July, study from September. Expect similar dates for 2027/28 and check the official site.

eligibility.q: Is your country a Stipendium Hungaricum sending partner, and are you a citizen of it (with no Hungarian citizenship)?
eligibility.no: Check the partner list in the Call for Applications. If your country is not listed you cannot apply; consider Türkiye Bursları or university scholarships.

eligibility.q: Can you meet your sending partner's own rules (e.g. Nigeria FSB: postgraduate applicants need a First Class or Second Class Upper degree, NYSC discharge or exemption, and age limits)?
eligibility.no: Nigerian applicants with a lower degree class or without NYSC discharge/exemption are unlikely to be nominated. Finish NYSC first or look at awards without nomination.

eligibility.q: Is the programme you want on the eligible programmes list for Stipendium Hungaricum?
eligibility.no: Only listed programmes qualify. Pick another programme from the list.

eligibility.q: Can you meet the language requirement of the programme (English-taught: as set by the university)?
eligibility.no: Book an English test early, or ask the university if your English-medium degree counts as proof.

eligibility.q: Can you cover extra costs? The stipend is partial (2026/27: HUF 43,700/month for master's plus HUF 40,000 housing contribution).
eligibility.no: Plan savings or part-time income. Nigeria's FSB supplement (BEA) ended from 2025/26, per the Hungarian Embassy in Abuja.

steps.title: Confirm eligibility and how nomination works
steps.why: This award has two gates: Hungary's call and your sending partner. Missing either one ends your application.
do: Open the stipendiumhungaricum.hu Apply page and read the Call for Applications PDF (the 2026/27 one shows the rules; the 2027/28 one replaces it in November).
Confirm your country is a sending partner and which levels it supports.
Nigeria: read the Hungarian Embassy Abuja FAQ. The Federal Scholarship Board (FSB) nominates and may set an earlier local deadline.

Read the FSB's last BEA advert to see its rules: postgraduate applicants need a First or Second Class Upper degree, NYSC discharge or exemption, and age 35 or under (master's) or 40 (PhD); undergraduates need 7 WAEC credits (A/B) and age 17–20.
Write down every requirement you meet and any you do not.
tips: FSB rules can change each year; confirm them once the new advert is out.
avoid: Applying only on the Hungarian portal and ignoring the FSB process.
check: I know my sending partner, its rules and that I meet them.

links.t: Hungarian Embassy Abuja: Stipendium Hungaricum FAQ

steps.title: Read the Call, the Application Guide and the Dos and Don'ts
steps.why: Most rejections are technical: wrong level, wrong programme type, missing file or unsubmitted form. These three documents prevent that.
do: Download the Call for Applications (BA/MA or PhD version) and the Application Guide.
Download the Checklist and the Dos and Don'ts PDF.
Highlight: deadline, two-programme rule, file size limit (4 MB), language rules, document list.
Note that you must not apply to two different levels in one application, or mix full-degree and partial programmes.
tips: Use a reliable email provider such as Gmail; the Dos and Don'ts advises this.
avoid: Paying agencies — the official guidance warns against unknown agents. Applying is free.
check: I have the Call, Guide, Checklist and Dos and Don'ts saved and read.

steps.title: Build your timeline
steps.why: You have two deadlines (Hungary's and your sending partner's), and the sending partner's may be earlier.
do: Put the expected Hungarian deadline (around 15 January 2027, 2 p.m. CET — confirm when the call is published) in your calendar.
Nigeria: check education.gov.ng regularly from November for the FSB advert and its closing date; last cycle it opened in early December and closed before the Hungarian deadline.
Set personal targets: programmes chosen by 30 November, documents scanned by 15 December, both applications submitted by 5 January.
Add the exam/interview window (March–May) and results (end June/early July).
tips: Work to whichever deadline is earlier.
avoid: Waiting for the call to be published before starting documents.
check: Both deadlines (or expected dates) are in my calendar with reminders.

steps.title: Choose your two programmes
steps.why: You may choose up to two programmes, in order. The first choice gets priority at the exam stage, and the order cannot be changed later.
do: Open the eligible full-degree programmes list (Excel) from the Apply page.
Filter by your level and field; note university, programme, language and entry requirements.
Visit each university's programme page to read the curriculum, entry rules and entrance exam format.
Pick two programmes in different universities if possible, ranked by real preference.
PhD: check doktori.hu, contact possible supervisors, and ask whether a supervisor statement is required.
tips: Choosing two programmes improves your chances, per the official Dos and Don'ts.
avoid: Choosing a partial/exchange programme when you want a full degree.
check: I have two eligible programmes, ranked, and I know each one's requirements.

steps.title: Register on the application system
steps.why: Everything is uploaded to apply.stipendiumhungaricum.hu. Registering early lets you see each field before the rush.
do: Go to apply.stipendiumhungaricum.hu and register with a reliable email.
Write down your login, password, applicant code and registration number.
Fill in personal details in English, exactly as on your passport.
Add your two programmes in your chosen order.
tips: Keep files under 4 MB each and clearly readable.
avoid: Typos in your email address — you will miss every message.
check: My account works and my programme choices are entered.

steps.title: Gather certificates, transcripts and ID
steps.why: The document list is strict. Missing items fail the technical check.
do: Open the 'Application documents' PDF for your level.
Master's: scan your bachelor's degree certificate and the transcript for all semesters (request it from Exams and Records).
Bachelor's: scan your secondary school (WAEC/NECO) certificate.
Scan your passport data page. If you do not have a passport yet, you can use a national ID and sign the declaration to obtain a passport by 1 August.
Add a recent photo (taken within the last 2 years).
Nigeria/FSB: also prepare your NIN slip and NYSC discharge or exemption certificate (postgraduate).
tips: Documents in English do not need translation for English-taught programmes.
avoid: Uploading only part of the transcript — all semesters are required.
check: Every mandatory document on the list is scanned under 4 MB.

steps.title: Get proof of English
steps.why: You must upload proof of language ability that meets the host university's standard.
do: Check each programme's English requirement on the university page.
If your degree was taught in English, ask whether an English-medium letter from your university is accepted (the official document list allows proof of prior education in the programme language).
If a test is needed, book IELTS/TOEFL/Duolingo now so the result arrives before December ends.
Scan the certificate or letter.
tips: Ask your university registry for a 'medium of instruction' letter early; it is cheaper than a test.
avoid: Assuming every university accepts the same proof.
check: I have accepted language proof for both programmes.

steps.title: Write your motivation letter
steps.why: It is a mandatory document and the one place you explain why these programmes and Hungary.
do: Open with the problem or interest that leads you to this field (a real example).
Show your preparation: degree, projects, work, NYSC, skills.
Explain why your first-choice programme and university, naming modules or research groups.
Explain why Hungary and how you will use the degree at home.

Format for the upload: at least 1 page, Times New Roman 12 pt, in English (or the programme's language). If the online form also has a motivation box, keep within the minimum and maximum character limits shown next to it.
Save as PDF and upload.
tips: Mention both programmes briefly if your letter is shared across choices.
avoid: A generic letter that could be sent to any country.
check: My letter meets the format rule and names specific programme features.

steps.prompt: Motivation for your chosen programmes, your background and your plans.
steps.limit: Minimum 1 page, Times New Roman 12 pt; online box shows its own min/max character limits (2026/27 Application Guide)

steps.title: PhD only: research plan, recommendation and supervisor statement
steps.why: Doctoral applicants must upload a research plan and a letter of recommendation; some doctoral schools also require a supervisor statement (by 15 March last cycle).
do: Read the PhD document list for what to upload.
Write a research plan of at least 2 pages (Times New Roman 12 pt) that matches the doctoral school's topics.
Ask an academic tutor or supervisor with a scientific degree for the mandatory letter of recommendation; it must be in by the main deadline.
Email the possible Hungarian supervisor with your plan and CV; ask whether a supervisor statement is needed.
Note the supervisor statement deadline (15 March in the 2026/27 cycle).
tips: Search topics and supervisors on doktori.hu before writing.
avoid: Sending the same email to dozens of professors.
check: I have a research plan and a supervisor who knows about my application.
steps.prompt: Research plan for your doctoral topic.
steps.limit: Research plan: minimum 2 pages, Times New Roman 12 pt (2026/27)

steps.title: Check whether recommendation letters are needed
steps.why: For BA/MA, recommendation letters are not on the mandatory list. The online form shows a 'References' section only when one of your programmes requires it. PhD applicants must always provide one (see the PhD step).
do: After entering your two programmes in the online system, look for a 'References' section — it appears only if a programme needs referees.
Read each university's programme page for extra document requests.
If needed, ask a lecturer who knows your work; send your CV and motivation letter.
Request a signed letter on letterhead two weeks before you plan to submit.
tips: Even if optional, a strong letter can help at the university stage.
check: I know whether my programmes require letters and have them if so.

steps.title: Submit to Hungary and to your sending partner
steps.why: Saving is not submitting. You also need the sending partner's application to be nominated.
do: In the online system, accept the 'Statement for Application'.
Check every section and upload; confirm the programme order is final.
Click submit and save the confirmation email.
Nigeria: complete the FSB application on education.gov.ng (click the FSB icon), uploading what it asks (last cycle: degree certificate, NIN slip, NYSC certificate).
Follow any extra FSB instructions (some years they ask for documents by email or hard copy).
tips: Submit at least a week early in case the portal is busy.
check: I have confirmation from both the Hungarian system and my sending partner.

steps.title: Prepare for the entrance exam or interview
steps.why: After nomination, universities test applicants (March–May) and score them out of 100. You need at least 56.
do: Watch your email for the university's invitation (often an online interview or written test).
Read the programme's admissions page for exam topics.
Revise core subjects from your degree.
Prepare answers on your motivation, background and plans.
Test your camera, internet and power backup for an online exam.
tips: Your first-choice programme examines you first; prepare most for it.
avoid: Missing the exam email because it went to spam.
check: I know my exam format and have revised for it.

steps.title: Accept the offer and prepare to move
steps.why: Results come end of June/early July. You must accept on time and arrange a residence permit before September.
do: Log in to the system, read your result, and accept within the stated deadline.
Get a medical certificate on the official template (dated after the date the call states) to show in Hungary.
Apply for a Hungarian residence permit for study at the embassy (Nigeria: Hungarian Embassy Abuja).
Plan finances: the stipend is partial, so budget for extra living costs.
Note the 2 compulsory free Hungarian language semesters for full-time BA/MA scholars.
tips: Start visa paperwork as soon as you accept.
check: I have accepted, booked my visa appointment, and planned my budget.

faq.a: No. The Hungarian application is free. Do not pay agents.

faq.q: Do I need a recommendation from the Hungarian Embassy?
faq.a: No. Nigerian applicants do not need Embassy recommendations, and the Embassy does not receive applications.

faq.q: Does the scholarship cover all my costs?
faq.a: No. The stipend and housing contribution are partial; plan extra funds.

faq.q: Can I apply for both a master's and a PhD?
Do I need a passport to apply?
faq.a: You can apply with a national ID and a signed declaration that you will get a passport by 1 August (2026/27 rule).

In 2026/27: HUF 43,700/month for bachelor's and master's plus HUF 40,000/month housing contribution; PhD HUF 140,000/month in the first phase and HUF 180,000 in the second. Check the new call for 2027/28 figures.
